metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Morris County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Historic Hapgood & Lake Park Section, Midvale & Briarcliff Parkway
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 2.76%, with an equalization ratio of 83.6%.
Public education represents 68.8% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 21.4%.
Average residential assessment is $877,800, producing an average annual tax bill of $24,227.28.

neighborhoods.name: Historic Hapgood & Lake Park Section
neighborhoods.character: Iconic early 20th-century Herbert Hapgood Craftsman homes, cedar shake colonials, and private lakefront beaches around 9 lakes
neighborhoods.description: Renowned planned residential park community with 9 man-made lakes, rustic stone bridges, and pristine Craftsman architecture.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: High assessment scale (k+ median assessment) with community paying over 68% of property taxes to its top-ranked school district.

neighborhoods.name: Midvale & Briarcliff Parkway
neighborhoods.character: Majestic tree-lined avenues with Hapgood Craftsman homes, colonials, and walkability to Briarcliff Middle School
neighborhoods.description: The quintessential Mountain Lakes parkway section, renowned for its architectural heritage and lake access.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Top-tier assessed valuations sustaining world-class public school education.

equityAnalysis.summary: Mountain Lakes Borough maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In Mountain Lakes Borough, homeowners pay an average of $24,227.28 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 9.69% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 83.6%, assessed values average ~83.6% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 68.8% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 21.4%, and Morris County claims 9.8%.
